episodes.title: The AI Rankings Just Got Reshuffled
episodes.about: A major overhaul of AI’s most-watched benchmark is reshuffling the model rankings and revealing a wider gap between open and closed models. NLW examines what the new tests reveal about real-world capabilities—and how much those rankings should matter when choosing your AI tools. In the headlines: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, Microsoft and Google report surging cloud revenue, and Nvidia faces broader antitrust scrutiny.
episodes.why: A benchmark overhaul just reshuffled the model rankings and widened the open-vs-closed gap; NLW works through what the new tests actually say about real-world capability, plus Gemini 4 Carbon in the headlines.

episodes.title: Taking on ServiceNow: Coding Agents the Rest of Us with Serval Co-Founder and CEO Jake Stauch
episodes.about: What happens when you put code-generation agents in the hands of enterprise IT teams? With Serval, you get a system where it's easy for everyone to be a builder. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Serval co-founder and CEO Jake Stauch to analyze his company’s direct challenge to ServiceNow as the enterprise automation and service management system of record. Jake explains that by building an AI platform for enterprise IT departments with Serval, users can safely build while still safeguarding permissions by strict deterministic approvals and an audit trail.
episodes.why: Serval gives enterprise IT teams coding agents to build their own automations, taking on ServiceNow with deterministic approvals and an audit trail as the guardrails.

episodes.title: Why AI Could Turn Small Law Firms Into Billion-Dollar Businesses
episodes.about: What happens when AI makes legal work cheap enough to take cases lawyers couldn't afford to touch before? Eve CEO Jay Madheswaran argues that AI won't just cut costs for law firms. It could expand access to legal representation by making an entirely new class of cases economically viable. Jay joins a16z General Partner Alex Rampell to explain how Eve is automating plaintiff law from the first client call through settlement, and why some firms are already using it to increase the number of clients each attorney can manage from roughly 100 to 500.
episodes.why: Out today: Eve automates plaintiff law from first client call to settlement, and firms using it are taking each attorney from roughly 100 clients to 500 — the argument is cheaper cases, not just cheaper lawyers.

episodes.title: 693. What’s Our Job as Humans Anymore?
episodes.about: It may just be being human. Stephen Dubner interviews A.I. performer Tilly Norwood to find out if we are as replaceable as we fear. (Part two of a two-part series.)
episodes.why: Part two of the AI-and-creativity series, out today: Dubner interviews A.I. performer Tilly Norwood, with SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin and Ethan Mollick among the sources, on whether performers are as replaceable as feared.

episodes.title: You Can't Escape AI. Here's How to Live With It.
episodes.about: AI is already doing much more than most of us realize. So what happens when it starts doing more of your work—and when it starts deciding what work you should hand over? I talk to Wharton professor Ethan Mollick, whose new book is Co-Existence, about the real AI update: why today’s models are radically more capable than the chatbots people remember; how to think about your job and your kids’ careers; why AI may break the system that trains young workers; and why agents that can cancel subscriptions, read your email, and take action on your behalf are both useful and unnerving.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Channels is Peter Kafka's show on media, tech, and culture, new here: Ethan Mollick on his new book Co-Existence, the training pipeline AI may break for young workers, and agents that cancel subscriptions and read your email for you.
